title: Unrestricted Database Modification via postgres_query_tool
description: The postgres_query_tool claims to execute read-only queries but passes arbitrary raw SQL directly to the PostgreSQL pool. An attacker can execute destructive SQL statements including DROP TABLE, INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE.
root_cause: executeNativeTool in savazai-console/src/lib/tool-gateway.ts does not validate SQL statements for read-only query operations, allowing arbitrary database mutations including table drop and unauthorized data modification.
intended_behavior: Execute safe read-only SQL queries against configured database connections.

trace.description: Receives user query dispatching postgres_query_tool with arbitrary query argument.
Passes untrusted SQL query string to executeDbQuery.
Executes raw unvalidated SQL statement directly via pool.query(query).

conditions.description: At least one database connection is registered in system configurations or passed in parameters.

execution.attacker_perspective: Attacker sends an orchestration or tool request invoking postgres_query_tool with a destructive SQL payload.
instructions: Trigger /api/orchestrator/test or /api/graph/invoke with a tool payload targeting postgres_query_tool.
Pass a mutating SQL command in the query parameter.
execution.expected_result: Database tables are dropped or modified.

remediation.strategy: Enforce strict read-only query validation, rejecting any statement starting with or containing mutating DDL/DML clauses.

code_changes.fixed_code: function isReadOnlyQuery(sql: string): boolean { const trimmed = sql.trim().toUpperCase(); const forbidden = [/\b(DROP|ALTER|TRUNCATE|DELETE|UPDATE|INSERT|GRANT|REVOKE|COPY|EXECUTE)\b/i]; return !forbidden.some(r => r.test(trimmed)) && /^(SELECT|EXPLAIN|SHOW|WITH)\b/i.test(trimmed); }

likelihood.reason: Any user or agent able to call postgres_query_tool can submit arbitrary SQL.

impact.reason: Full database tampering, loss of data integrity, and denial of service.

confidence.reason: Confirmed by source code inspection of executeDbQuery in tool-gateway.ts.

title: Server-Side Request Forgery via Custom Webhook Tool Invocation
description: The custom webhook tool execution gateway accepts arbitrary URLs without verifying that destination IP addresses are outside private network ranges, loopbacks, and cloud metadata endpoints.
root_cause: callCustomWebhook in savazai-console/src/lib/tool-gateway.ts does not validate destination URLs against private IP and link-local ranges, allowing attackers to access internal intranet infrastructure and cloud metadata services.
intended_behavior: Allow outbound webhook notifications exclusively to public external internet APIs.

trace.description: Receives tool invocation request for custom webhook or fallback tool.
Routes tool execution with URL argument to callCustomWebhook.
Performs unconstrained HTTP fetch to arbitrary user-supplied URL.

conditions.description: Application is hosted in cloud or internal environment with reachable private endpoints or metadata services.

execution.attacker_perspective: Attacker triggers custom webhook execution with an internal destination IP.
instructions: Observe internal responses returned in tool execution result.
execution.expected_result: Cloud metadata or internal service response returned to caller.

remediation.strategy: Validate destination URLs against loopback, private RFC1918 subnets, and link-local metadata addresses before initiating HTTP requests.

code_changes.fixed_code: function isSafeExternalUrl(urlStr: string): boolean { try { const parsed = new URL(urlStr); if (parsed.protocol !== 'http:' && parsed.protocol !== 'https:') return false; const host = parsed.hostname.toLowerCase(); if (host === 'localhost' || host === '127.0.0.1' || host === '::1' || host === '169.254.169.254') return false; if (host.startsWith('10.') || host.startsWith('192.168.') || /^172\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[0-1])\./.test(host)) return false; return true; } catch { return false; } }

likelihood.reason: Webhook tool execution is readily accessible via tool dispatcher.

impact.reason: Access to cloud instance metadata, internal databases, and private services.

title: Unauthenticated Compliance Policy Override in Governance API
description: The PUT endpoint for compliance rules allows any unauthenticated HTTP client to overwrite data masking, keyword blocking, and PII protection policies.
root_cause: PUT in savazai-console/src/app/api/governance/compliance/route.ts does not authenticate the requesting session, allowing unauthenticated attackers to overwrite or disable data compliance and PII masking configurations.
intended_behavior: Only authenticated administrative users should be able to update compliance policies.

trace.description: Receives HTTP PUT request with arbitrary ComplianceConfig payload.
Deletes existing agentflow compliance rules from database.
Inserts attacker-supplied compliance configuration without authorization check.

execution.attacker_perspective: Attacker issues direct HTTP PUT request to /api/governance/compliance with empty entity rules.
instructions: Send PUT request to /api/governance/compliance with disabled PII rules.
Observe 200 OK response and cleared compliance table.
execution.expected_result: PII masking is disabled across all subsequent agent interactions.

remediation.strategy: Enforce Better-Auth session verification on PUT /api/governance/compliance to restrict policy modifications to authenticated administrators.

code_changes.fixed_code: const session = await auth.api.getSession({ headers: await headers() }); if (!session) { return new Response(JSON.stringify({ error: 'Unauthorized' }), { status: 401 }); }

impact.reason: Complete bypass of PII redaction and compliance governance across the platform.

confidence.reason: Confirmed by inspection of PUT handler in compliance route.ts.

title: Insecure Script Path Traversal in Python Sandbox Runner
description: The python-runner utility accepts arbitrary script paths without verifying that they resolve within authorized script directories, allowing traversal outside intended boundaries.
root_cause: runPython in src/utils/python-runner.ts does not restrict the scriptPath argument to allowed script directories, allowing directory traversal and arbitrary script execution.
intended_behavior: Only execute verified Python scripts located in scripts/ or src/skills/ directories.

trace.description: Receives graph execution trigger with active tools and parameters.
Passes script path to runPython utility.
Spawns python3 process with unconstrained path.

conditions.description: Python execution environment is configured on host.

execution.attacker_perspective: Attacker crafts tool parameters referencing traversal paths like '../../tmp/malicious.py'.
instructions: Invoke python runner with relative path escaping scripts directory.

remediation.strategy: Validate and resolve scriptPath ensuring it resides strictly within allowed directories (scripts/ or src/skills/).

code_changes.fixed_code: const resolved = resolve(process.cwd(), scriptPath); const allowedDirs = [resolve(process.cwd(), 'scripts'), resolve(process.cwd(), 'src/skills')]; if (!allowedDirs.some(dir => resolved.startsWith(dir))) throw new Error('Unauthorized script path');

likelihood.reason: Requires triggering tool execution with manipulated script path.

impact.reason: Execution confined to Python runtime on host/container.

confidence.reason: Confirmed in runPython implementation in python-runner.ts.
